newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - PHILIPS TO CUT STAKE IN ASM LITHOGRAPHY.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - PHILIPS TO CUT STAKE IN ASM LITHOGRAPHY.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday it planned to cut its minority stake in semi-conductor equipment maker ASM Lithography Holding NV in a move which could raise around 400 million guilders.
Separately, ASM Lithography reported that 1996 net earnings jumped 66 percent to 217.7 million guilders from 131.4 million.
"Philips intends to offer 3,950,000 ordinary shares...in an international offering," ASML and Philips said in a joint statement accompanying ASML's results.
A Philips spokesman said Credit Suisse First Boston would be book runner, co-ordinating the sale of the shares which would bring Philips' 35 percent holding down to 24 percent.
"It is expected that the pricing of the shares will be announced on January 30," Philips spokesman Ben Geerts said, declining to give further details.
"Philips will use the proceeds of its offering for general corporate purposes. ASML will not receive any of the proceeds from the sale of the shares by Philips," the two firms said.

Geerts said the offering would be the third sale of ASML shares since 1995, when it cut its 100 percent stake to 55 percent. It followed that up with another cut in 1996, but has a commitment to keep its stake at 24 percent until March 2000.

"The offer is part of the strategy formulated by Philips when we first floated part of our stake in 1995. We said at the time that producing equipment for the semi-conductor industry was not our core business," said Geerts.
He denied that the proposed sale of more ASML shares was part of the strategy announced by new Philips chairman Cor Boonstra last October.
Boonstra then vowed to weed out the company's loss-making and underperforming "bleeders".

Since October Philips has announced a string of changes including moving to a passive minority shareholding in German consumer electronics firm Grundig, cutting back head office staff and winding up its Superclub home entertainments business.
"Today's move is absolutely not part of the bleeders strategy because ASML makes good profits," said Geerts.
ASML said in its results statement that its profits soared because of increases in the volume of sales and in average selling prices versus 1995.
The rise in ASM Lithography's 1996 earnings was at the lower end of analysts' forecasts of 210-241 million guilders.

ASM Lithography also announced plans for a two-for-one share split, saying it would seek shareholder approval for the move on April 3. Presenting the results, ASML chief executive Willem Maris told a news conference the company increased market share to an estimated 19 percent in 1996, up from 17 percent in 1995.

"We've won market share," Maris told reporters. "Our strategic target is 1/3 of the market and second position (up from a current third) in the market place," he said, but declined to give a time-frame.

The company, which has a dual listing on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange and U.S. Nasdaq, said that after last year's slowdown in the semiconductor industry the outlook for the first 1997 half was "moderate" but could pick up in the second.

"While we expect that the first half of 1997 will be consistent with the moderate forecast of the semiconductor equipment industry, we anticipate that demand for semiconductor equipment may strengthen in the second half," ASM Litho said.
Sales rose to 1.33 billion guilders from 920 million.

On the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, ASM Lithography shares opened a guilder lower on the news at 110.00, falling heavily to 104.00 in the first 90 minutes of trade, but later rallied to be five guilders down at 106.00 guilders.
